# Castle sequence catalog

## What this is

This page catalogs the sequences that castles produce, organized by the castle family each one counts rather than by OEIS A-number. Each row gives first terms, a recurrence or generating function (g.f.), its growth constant, and the entry of the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS) it equals, at the stated offset; "-" means no entry is listed.[^1]

This page and [[oeis-index](pages/oeis-index.md)] are generated by `bin/generate-sequence-pages.py` from one data file, `config/castle-sequences.tsv`: this page shows its rows by castle family, in the order and with the definitions of `config/castle-families.tsv`, and the index shows its A-numbers with the pages that cite them. [[oeis-cross-referencing](pages/oeis-cross-referencing.md)] describes the checks a match must pass, [[oeis-mining-pe502](pages/oeis-mining-pe502.md)] collects the castle counts matched to OEIS entries, and [[oeis-height2-hyperbolic-castles](pages/oeis-height2-hyperbolic-castles.md)] proves the height-2 rows.

The symbols are those of [[castle-notation](pages/castle-notation.md)]: `A^e(w, h)` and `A^o(w, h)` count the castles of width `w` and height `h` with an even and an odd number of blocks. A skyline on `{1, …, h}` need not reach height `h`, so a count of skylines on `{1, …, h}` is a count of castles of every height up to `h`.

## OEIS entries proved on other pages

These identities are stated and proved on the pages cited; the section *Catalog* gives the terms of most of them.

- [[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)]: [A005251](https://oeis.org/A005251), the number of tree castles of area `n`, the number of cells, with the height unrestricted: castles in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2, which is exactly when the castle graph (cells as vertices, joined when they share a side) is a tree ([[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)], [[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)]). Read left to right, the column heights of a tree castle are a composition of `n` (an ordered sum of positive parts) with no two neighboring parts at least 2, and every such composition is a tree castle (`n = 1…`): `A005251(n+2)`; [A005251](https://oeis.org/A005251), the number of binary strings of length `N` with no factor `010`, that is, no three consecutive symbols `0, 1, 0`. These strings are a reading of the tree castles (castles in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2): the gap map writes a tree castle of area `n` as a string of length `N = n − 1`, each column of height `c` becoming `c − 1` zeros and neighboring columns separated by a single `1`, and it is a bijection from the tree castles of area `n` onto these strings ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)]) (`N = 0…`): `A005251(N+3)`; [A005251](https://oeis.org/A005251), the number `W_1(N)` of binary words of length `N` with no isolated `1`, so that every run of 1s has length at least 2. `W_1` is the case `m = 1` of the words `W_m` of [[hardin-word-identity](pages/hardin-word-identity.md)] (words in `{0, …, m}^N` in which every nonzero letter is at most one of its neighbors), whose cases `m = 2, 3, 4` are Hardin's OEIS entries. The words are a reading of the tree castles (castles in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2): the column map sends a tree castle of area `n` to a word of length `N = n`, a column of height 1 becoming `0` and a column of height `c ≥ 2` becoming `1^c`, one-to-one and onto ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)], [[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)]) (`N = 1…`): `A005251(N+2)`; [A005251](https://oeis.org/A005251), the number of compositions of `m` (ordered ways of writing `m` as a sum of positive parts) with no part equal to 2. They are a reading of the tree castles (castles in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2): the leading-column map puts a column of height 1 in front of a tree castle of area `n` and merges each column of height 1 followed by a column of height `j ≥ 2` into one part `1 + j`, which gives a composition of `m = n + 1` with no part 2, one-to-one and onto ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)], [[tree-castle-by-area](pages/tree-castle-by-area.md)]) (`m = 1…`): `A005251(m+1)`; [A005251](https://oeis.org/A005251), the number of skylines of width `w` with every column between 1 and 2 and tower spacing at least 2: in every row, each run of empty cells that has filled cells on both sides is at least 2 columns wide ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)]). Such a skyline need not reach height 2, so this counts the castles of width `w` and of every height up to 2 with that spacing; the castles of height exactly 2 among them number this count minus 1, the flat row `(1, …, 1)`. The gap map followed by the complement carries the tree castles of area `w + 1` (castles in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2) one to one onto these skylines ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)]) (`w = 1…`): `A005251(w+3)`; [A005251](https://oeis.org/A005251), the sum of `(−1)^{blocks}` over the towers of height at most 6 on a base of length `L` whose last column has even height, written `P_even(6, L)` (the even sector of the signed tower count), divided by `2^L`; a tower being what remains of a castle when its bottom row, which is one block, is removed: `L` columns of heights 0 to 6, all of height 0 allowed ([[signed-tower-count](pages/signed-tower-count.md)], [[tower-parity-sectors](pages/tower-parity-sectors.md)]). It is a signed sum, and it equals a count: `P_even(6, L) = 2^L W_1(L + 1)`, with `W_1(N)` the number of binary strings of length `N` with no isolated 1, so the quotient is the number of tree castles of area `L + 1` (castles with no two neighboring columns both of height at least 2), proved by a change of basis between transfer matrices ([[hardin-word-identity](pages/hardin-word-identity.md)], [[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)]) (`L = 0…`): `A005251(L+3)`.

A strip need not reach height 4, so this counts the Hilbert castles of every height up to 4 together; they number `2F_{2w+1}` for `w ≥ 1`. Relabeling the heights by `1 ↦ 3`, `2 ↦ 1`, `3 ↦ 4`, `4 ↦ 2` turns the 1-smooth rule (neighbors differ by at most 1) into the Hilbert rule, so the same numbers count the 1-smooth strips on four heights with any first column, the OEIS reading (`w = 0…`): `A126358(w)`; [A000225](https://oeis.org/A000225), the number of Hilbert castles of width `w` and height 3: castles of height 3 in which no two neighboring columns differ in height by exactly 1 ([[hilbert-castles](pages/hilbert-castles.md)]). A column of height 2 can stand only next to another of height 2, so these are the skylines on `{1, 3}` other than the flat row `(1, …, 1)`, `2^w − 1` of them, and every one has an odd number of blocks (`w = 1…`): `A000225(w)`.
- [[castle-classification-shape](pages/castle-classification-shape.md)]: [A019274](https://oeis.org/A019274), the number of 2-disparate castles of height exactly 4 and width `w`; an m-disparate castle is a castle whose neighboring columns differ in height by at least `m`, here at least 2 ([[castle-classification-shape](pages/castle-classification-shape.md)], paragraph *m-disparate castles*). For `w ≥ 2` they number `2(F_{w+2} − 1)`, and for every `m ≥ 2` the m-disparate castles of height `m + 2` have the same counts (`w = 1…`): `A019274(w + 2)`.
- [[kolmogorov-castles](pages/kolmogorov-castles.md)]: [A000984](https://oeis.org/A000984), the number of Kolmogorov castles of width `2n + 1`, of every height, one for each merged order, `C(2n, n)`: a Kolmogorov castle is the skyline `c_i = 1 + |a_i − b_i|` of a merged order of two samples of `n` values each, `a_i` and `b_i` counting the values of each sample among the first `i − 1`, with each peak (maximal run of columns of height at least 2) marked by the sample ahead on it ([[kolmogorov-castles](pages/kolmogorov-castles.md)]) (`n = 0…`): `A000984(n)`; [A000079](https://oeis.org/A000079), the number of Kolmogorov castles (castles of merged orders of two samples of `n` values each, [[kolmogorov-castles](pages/kolmogorov-castles.md)]) of width `2n + 1` and height exactly 2, `2^n`: height 2 means that the lead of one sample over the other never exceeds 1 (`n = 1…`): `A000079(n)`; [A056182](https://oeis.org/A056182), the number of Kolmogorov castles (castles of merged orders of two samples of `n` values each, [[kolmogorov-castles](pages/kolmogorov-castles.md)]) of width `2n + 1` and height exactly 3, `2(3^{n−1} − 2^{n−1})`: the lead of one sample over the other reaches 2 and never exceeds 2 (`n = 1…`): `A056182(n − 1)`; [A000108](https://oeis.org/A000108), the number of Kolmogorov castles (castles of merged orders of two samples of `n` values each, [[kolmogorov-castles](pages/kolmogorov-castles.md)]) of width `2n + 1` with no peak marked `X`, the merged orders in which the first sample is never ahead: one for each Dyck-path castle of width `2n + 1` (columns step up or down by 1, both end columns at height 1), with every peak marked `Y`, the Catalan number `C_n` (`n = 0…`): `A000108(n)`.
- [[signed-tower-count](pages/signed-tower-count.md)]: [A146559](https://oeis.org/A146559), the signed tower count `P(1, L)`, the sum of `(−1)^{blocks}` over the towers of height at most 1 on a base of length `L`, which are the binary strings of length `L` with the runs of 1s as blocks (a tower being what remains of a castle when its bottom row, which is one block, is removed: `L` columns of heights 0 to 1, all of height 0 allowed), [[signed-tower-count](pages/signed-tower-count.md)]. It is a signed sum, equal to `Re((1+i)^{L+1})`; `1 − P(1, w)` is the number of castles of width `w` and height 2 with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number (`L = 0…`): `A146559(L+1)`.

The height-2 columns of such a castle form a binary string of length `w` ending in 1, and the signed difference is `−P_odd(1, w)`, minus the sum of `(−1)^{blocks}` over the towers of height at most 1 on a base of length `w` whose last column has height 1, which is the imaginary part of `(1+i)^w` ([[signed-tower-count](pages/signed-tower-count.md)], [[tower-parity-sectors](pages/tower-parity-sectors.md)]) (`w = 1…`): `A009545(w)`.
- [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)]: [A352116](https://oeis.org/A352116), the absolute value `|P(k, 4)|` of the signed tower count at base length 4, as a function of the tower height bound `k`: `P(k, 4)` is the sum of `(−1)^{blocks}` over the towers of height at most `k` on a base of 4 columns (a tower being what remains of a castle when its bottom row is removed, columns of heights 0 to `k`). It is not a count; `P(k, 4)` has the sign `(−1)^k`, and its absolute values are the partial sums of the odd triangular numbers ([[signed-tower-k-direction](pages/signed-tower-k-direction.md)], [[castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk](pages/castle-eigenvalue-oeis-crosswalk.md)]) (`k = 0…`): `A352116(k + 1)`.
- [[oeis-height2-hyperbolic-castles](pages/oeis-height2-hyperbolic-castles.md)]: [A038505](https://oeis.org/A038505), `A^e(w, 2)`, the number of castles of width `w` and height 2 with an even number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row); the height-2 columns form a binary string, and the castle has one block more than the string has runs of 1s ([[oeis-height2-hyperbolic-castles](pages/oeis-height2-hyperbolic-castles.md)]) (`w = 1…`): `A038505(w + 1)`; [A038503](https://oeis.org/A038503), `A^o(w, 2)`, the number of castles of width `w` and height 2 with an odd number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row); the height-2 columns form a binary string, and the castle has one block more than the string has runs of 1s ([[oeis-height2-hyperbolic-castles](pages/oeis-height2-hyperbolic-castles.md)]) (`w = 1…`): `A038503(w + 1) − 1`.
- [[tower-narayana-polynomial](pages/tower-narayana-polynomial.md)]: [A005408](https://oeis.org/A005408), the number of castles of width 2, any height, with `b + 1` blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row); removing the bottom row, which is one block, leaves the towers on a base of 2 columns with `b` blocks ([[tower-narayana-polynomial](pages/tower-narayana-polynomial.md)]) (`b = 0…`): `A005408(b)`; [A005891](https://oeis.org/A005891), the number of castles of width 3, any height, with `b + 1` blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row); removing the bottom row, which is one block, leaves the towers on a base of 3 columns with `b` blocks ([[tower-narayana-polynomial](pages/tower-narayana-polynomial.md)]) (`b = 0…`): `A005891(b)`; [A063490](https://oeis.org/A063490), the number of castles of width 4, any height, with `b + 1` blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row); removing the bottom row, which is one block, leaves the towers on a base of 4 columns with `b` blocks ([[tower-narayana-polynomial](pages/tower-narayana-polynomial.md)]) (`b = 0…`): `A063490(b + 1)`; [A160747](https://oeis.org/A160747), the number of castles of width 5, any height, with `b + 1` blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row); removing the bottom row, which is one block, leaves the towers on a base of 5 columns with `b` blocks ([[tower-narayana-polynomial](pages/tower-narayana-polynomial.md)]) (`b = 0…`): `A160747(b)`; [A001263](https://oeis.org/A001263), the Narayana numbers `N(L, k) = (1/L) C(L, k) C(L, k − 1)`, the number of Dyck paths of semilength `L` with `k` peaks ([[narayana-numbers](pages/narayana-numbers.md)]). They count towers by blocks: removing the bottom row of a castle, which is one block, leaves a tower, and the towers of any height on a base of length `L` with `b` blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) number `T̂(L, b) = Σ_k N(L, k) C(b + L − k, L − 1)` ([[tower-narayana-polynomial](pages/tower-narayana-polynomial.md)]).
- [[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)]: [A001045](https://oeis.org/A001045), the number `T_3(w)` of tree skylines of width `w` and height at most 3: skylines `(c_1, …, c_w)` with every `c_i` in `{1, 2, 3}` in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2 ([[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)]). A tree skyline need not reach height 3, so this counts the tree castles of every height up to 3 together, and the tree castles of height exactly 3 number `T_3(w) − T_2(w)`; these are the Jacobsthal numbers (`w = 1…`): `A001045(w + 2)`; [A006130](https://oeis.org/A006130), the number `T_4(w)` of tree skylines of width `w` and height at most 4: skylines `(c_1, …, c_w)` with every `c_i` in `{1, 2, 3, 4}` in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2 ([[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)]). A tree skyline need not reach height 4, so this counts the tree castles of every height up to 4 together, and the tree castles of height exactly 4 number `T_4(w) − T_3(w)` (`w = 1…`): `A006130(w + 1)`; [A006131](https://oeis.org/A006131), the number `T_5(w)` of tree skylines of width `w` and height at most 5: skylines `(c_1, …, c_w)` with every `c_i` in `{1, 2, 3, 4, 5}` in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2 ([[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)]). - [[fibonacci-castle](pages/fibonacci-castle.md)]: [A000071](https://oeis.org/A000071), the number of Fibonacci castles of width `w`: castles of height 2 with no two neighboring columns of height 2 ([[fibonacci-castle](pages/fibonacci-castle.md)]). They are the tree castles of height exactly 2, the castles of height 2 whose castle graph (cells as vertices, joined when they share a side) is a tree ([[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)]), and they number `F_{w+2} − 1`, one less than the skylines on `{1, 2}` with no two neighboring 2s (`w = 1…`): `A000071(w + 2)`.
- [[castle-by-area](pages/castle-by-area.md)]: [A001523](https://oeis.org/A001523), the number of convex castles of area `n`, the number of cells, of any width and height; a convex castle is a castle whose skyline rises weakly to its tallest column and then falls weakly ([[convex-castle](pages/convex-castle.md)]). Reading the column heights left to right makes a castle of area `n` a composition of `n`, so these are the weakly unimodal compositions of `n` ([[weakly-unimodal-composition](pages/weakly-unimodal-composition.md)]), the stacks of polyomino theory (`n = 1…`): `A001523(n)`; [A115981](https://oeis.org/A115981), the number of non-convex castles of area `n`, the number of cells: castles whose skyline does not rise weakly and then fall weakly. Reading the column heights in order makes a castle of area `n` a composition of `n`, and the convex ones are the weakly unimodal compositions, so this is `2^{n−1} − A001523(n)`, the compositions of `n` that cannot be viewed as stacks ([[castle-by-area](pages/castle-by-area.md)]) (`n = 1…`): `A115981(n)`; [A332578](https://oeis.org/A332578), the number of vee castles of area `n`, the number of cells, of any width and height; a vee castle is a castle whose skyline falls weakly to its lowest column and then rises weakly ([[castle-by-area](pages/castle-by-area.md)]). Reading the column heights left to right makes a castle of area `n` a composition of `n`, so these are the compositions of `n` whose negation is unimodal (`n = 1…`): `A332578(n)`.
- [[euler-castles](pages/euler-castles.md)]: [A000009](https://oeis.org/A000009), the number of Euler castles (castles whose columns fall by 0 or 1 at each step and end at height 1, such as `(3, 3, 2, 1, 1)`, [[euler-castles](pages/euler-castles.md)]) of area `n`, the number of cells. An Euler castle has one block per row, so these are the partitions of `n` into an even number of distinct parts (`n = 1…`): `A067661(n)`; [A067659](https://oeis.org/A067659), the number of Euler castles (castles whose columns fall by 0 or 1 at each step and end at height 1, such as `(3, 3, 2, 1, 1)`, [[euler-castles](pages/euler-castles.md)]) of area `n` with an odd number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. An Euler castle has one block per row, so these are the partitions of `n` into an odd number of distinct parts (`n = 1…`): `A067659(n)`; [A010815](https://oeis.org/A010815), the number of Euler castles (castles whose columns fall by 0 or 1 at each step and end at height 1, such as `(3, 3, 2, 1, 1)`, [[euler-castles](pages/euler-castles.md)]) of area `n` with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row (one per row on an Euler castle). - [[totient-castles](pages/totient-castles.md)]: [A000071](https://oeis.org/A000071), the number of totient castles of height exactly 2 and width `w`, totient castles being castles whose neighboring columns have coprime heights, `gcd(c_i, c_{i+1}) = 1` ([[totient-castles](pages/totient-castles.md)]). These are the Pell-Lucas numbers, as many as the 1-smooth strips on `{1, 2, 3}`, whose neighboring columns differ by at most 1 ([[pell-castle-strip](pages/pell-castle-strip.md)]) (`w = 1…`): `A001333(w + 1)`; [A167606](https://oeis.org/A167606), the number of totient castles of area `n`, the number of cells, of any width and height, totient castles being castles whose neighboring columns have coprime heights, `gcd(c_i, c_{i+1}) = 1` ([[totient-castles](pages/totient-castles.md)]). Reading the column heights left to right makes a castle of area `n` a composition of `n`, so these are the compositions of `n` whose neighboring parts are coprime (`n = 1…`): `A167606(n)`.

it counts periods, and the sign-alternating orbital castles of order `2m` and height `h` (differences alternating in sign) number `C(h − 1, 2m − 1) · 2m` times it (`m = 1…`): `A000182(m)`.
- [[konigsberg-castles](pages/konigsberg-castles.md)]: [A034856](https://oeis.org/A034856), the number of open-stroke castles (castles that can be traced in one open stroke, and in no closed one, crossing exactly once each side shared by two cells and each side between a bottom cell and the ground, [[konigsberg-castles](pages/konigsberg-castles.md)]) of height `h` and odd width, all odd widths together. - [[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]: [A000225](https://oeis.org/A000225), the width of the von Neumann castle `vN(n)`, the castle of the ordinal `n = {0, 1, …, n − 1}`, where the castle of a set is a bottom block carrying the castles of its members left to right with one empty column between neighbors, for example `vN(2) = (2, 1, 3)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]). It is a statistic of one castle for each `n` (`n = 0…`): `A057711(n + 1)`; [A000079](https://oeis.org/A000079), the number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) of the von Neumann castle `vN(n)`, the castle of the ordinal `n = {0, 1, …, n − 1}`, where the castle of a set is a bottom block carrying the castles of its members left to right with one empty column between neighbors, for example `vN(2) = (2, 1, 3)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]), with `C(n, d)` of them in row `d + 1`, the nodes of the binomial tree of order `n`. It is a statistic of one castle for each `n`; since `2^n` is even for `n ≥ 1`, every `vN(n)` from `n = 1` has an even number of blocks (`n = 0…`): `A000079(n)`; [A000108](https://oeis.org/A000108), the number of alternating castles with `b` blocks, castles of odd width with `c_1 > c_2 < c_3 > ⋯ < c_w`. Its castle is a bottom block carrying the castles of its members from left to right, in increasing Ackermann code, one empty column between neighbors, and the empty set's castle is the single cell `(1)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]). Distinct sets have distinct castles and each block is one pair of braces of the set written out in full, so these are the sets with `b` pairs of braces, the rooted identity trees with `b` nodes (`b = 1…`): `A004111(b)`; [A116549](https://oeis.org/A116549), the number of blocks of the Ackermann castle `ack(m)`, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. It is a statistic of one castle for each `m`, equal to the number of pairs of braces in the set written out in full (`m = 0…`): `A116549(m)`; [A033922](https://oeis.org/A033922), the width of the Ackermann castle `ack(m)`. The Ackermann castle `ack(m)` is the castle of the hereditarily finite set with Ackermann code `m`, the set whose members are the sets coded by the positions of the 1s in the binary form of `m`; the castle is a bottom block carrying the castles of the members from left to right in increasing code, one empty column between neighbors, and the empty set's castle is the single cell `(1)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]). It is a statistic of one castle for each `m`: the width is `2·leaves(m) − 1`, with `leaves(m)` the number of leaves of the set's membership tree, the base-2 digital convolution sequence A033922(`m`) (`m = 0…`): `2a(m) − 1`; [A010096](https://oeis.org/A010096), the height of the Ackermann castle `ack(m)`. The Ackermann castle `ack(m)` is the castle of the hereditarily finite set with Ackermann code `m`, the set whose members are the sets coded by the positions of the 1s in the binary form of `m`; the castle is a bottom block carrying the castles of the members from left to right in increasing code, one empty column between neighbors, and the empty set's castle is the single cell `(1)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]). It is a statistic of one castle for each `m`: the height is 1 plus the rank of the set, which is the iterated base-2 logarithm A010096(`m`), also `1 + A230864(m + 1)` (`m = 1…`): `A010096(m) + 1`; [A372325](https://oeis.org/A372325), the numbers `m`, in increasing order, whose Ackermann castle `ack(m)` has an odd number of blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row, which are the `m` with A116549(`m`) odd. The Ackermann castle `ack(m)` is the castle of the hereditarily finite set with Ackermann code `m`, the set whose members are the sets coded by the positions of the 1s in the binary form of `m`; the castle is a bottom block carrying the castles of the members from left to right in increasing code, one empty column between neighbors, and the empty set's castle is the single cell `(1)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]). They are the terms of A372325, the numbers whose binary form has an even number of 1s at positions that are themselves terms (`n = 1…`): `A372325(n)`.
- [[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)]: [A000108](https://oeis.org/A000108), the number of brick-wall castles (castles on the hexagonal tiling read as a brick wall: a full bottom row of `w` bricks, every higher brick resting on both bricks below it, a block being a maximal run of bricks in one row, [[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)]) of width `w`, the bottom-row length; they are the fountains of coins counted by bottom row (`w = 1…`): `A000108(w)`; [A080936](https://oeis.org/A080936), the number of brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) of width `w` (bottom row of `w` bricks) and height exactly `h` (`h` rows of bricks); they correspond to the Dyck paths of semilength `w` and height `h` (`w = 1…`): `A080936(w, h)`; [A001263](https://oeis.org/A001263), the number of brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) of width `w` (bottom row of `w` bricks) with `b` blocks, a block being a maximal run of bricks in one row: the Narayana numbers `N(w, b)`, since a castle with `b` blocks matches a Dyck path of semilength `w` with `w + 1 − b` peaks (`b = 1…`): `A001263(w, b)`; [A004148](https://oeis.org/A004148), the number of brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) of semi-perimeter `s = w + b`, the width plus the number of blocks, which is the semi-perimeter (half the boundary length) of the square-grid castle that the brick-wall castle shears to; that shear gives the castles whose columns drop by at most 1 and end at height 1, which are counted by the peakless Motzkin paths (`s = 2…`): `A004148(s−1)`; [A000225](https://oeis.org/A000225), the number of brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) of width `w` (bottom row of `w` bricks) and height exactly 2 (`w = 2…`): `A000225(w−1)`; [A038505](https://oeis.org/A038505), the number `A^e_brick(w, 2)` of brick-wall castles ([[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], castles on the brick wall whose every higher brick rests on both bricks below it) of width `w` and height exactly 2 with an even number of blocks; after the shear, these have an odd number of runs of height-2 columns after the first column (`w = 2…`): `A038505(w)`.
- [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]: [A006318](https://oeis.org/A006318), the number of keystone castles of width `w`, any height: castles on the triangular tiling with a full bottom row of `w` up triangles and the `w − 1` down triangles between them, every higher triangle supported so that nothing overhangs ([[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]); the top outline of each is a large Schröder path of semilength `w − 1`, a path of up, down and flat steps that never goes below its base line (`w = 1…`): `A006318(w−1)`; [A088617](https://oeis.org/A088617), the number of keystone castles of width `w` (`w` up triangles in the bottom row), any height, with `b` blocks, a block being a maximal run of triangles in one row ([[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]) (`b = 1…`): `A088617(w − 1, b − 1)`; [A001006](https://oeis.org/A001006), the number of keystone castles (castles on the triangular tiling with a full bottom row of `w` up triangles and the `w − 1` down triangles between them, every higher triangle supported so that nothing overhangs, [[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]), any width and height, whose width plus number of blocks is `s`, a block being a maximal run of triangles in one row. Reading the outline's large Schröder path with every step of length 1 makes these the Motzkin paths of length `s − 2` (`s = 2…`): `A001006(s−2)`; [A027941](https://oeis.org/A027941), the number of keystone castles of width `w` and height 2, two rows of triangles ([[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]) (`w = 2…`): `A027941(w−1)`; [A393774](https://oeis.org/A393774), the number of keystone castles with `n` cells, a cell being one triangle, any width and height ([[keystone-castles](pages/keystone-castles.md)]) (`n = 1…`): `A393774(n−1)`.
- [[hardin-word-identity](pages/hardin-word-identity.md)]: [A202882](https://oeis.org/A202882), the number of words of length `n` over the letters `{0, 1, 2}` in which every nonzero letter is at most one of its neighbors (no nonzero letter is a strict local maximum, with a virtual 0 beyond each end), Hardin's words `W_2(n)`. It is not itself a castle count. By the Hardin word identity it is a signed tower count, `W_2(L + 1) = P_even(10, L)/2^L`, where `P_even(10, L)` is the number of towers (castles with their bottom row removed) of height at most 10 on a base of length `L` whose last column has even height, each counted +1 or −1 by the parity of its number of blocks ([[hardin-word-identity](pages/hardin-word-identity.md)]). It also counts the skylines of width `n − 1` with every column of height 1 to 3 and tower spacing at least 2, meaning every run of empty cells in a row between two filled cells has length at least 2; these need not reach height 3, so they are the castles of every height up to 3 with that spacing ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)]); [A203094](https://oeis.org/A203094), the number of words of length `n` over the letters `{0, 1, 2, 3}` in which every nonzero letter is at most one of its neighbors (no nonzero letter is a strict local maximum, with a virtual 0 beyond each end), Hardin's words `W_3(n)`. It is not itself a castle count. By the Hardin word identity it is a signed tower count, `W_3(L + 1) = P_even(14, L)/2^L`, where `P_even(14, L)` is the number of towers (castles with their bottom row removed) of height at most 14 on a base of length `L` whose last column has even height, each counted +1 or −1 by the parity of its number of blocks ([[hardin-word-identity](pages/hardin-word-identity.md)]). It also counts the skylines of width `n − 1` with every column of height 1 to 4 and tower spacing at least 2, meaning every run of empty cells in a row between two filled cells has length at least 2; these need not reach height 4, so they are the castles of every height up to 4 with that spacing ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)]); [A203184](https://oeis.org/A203184), the number of words of length `n` over the letters `{0, 1, …, 4}` in which every nonzero letter is at most one of its neighbors (no nonzero letter is a strict local maximum, with a virtual 0 beyond each end), Hardin's words `W_4(n)`. It is not itself a castle count. By the Hardin word identity it is a signed tower count, `W_4(L + 1) = P_even(18, L)/2^L`, where `P_even(18, L)` is the number of towers (castles with their bottom row removed) of height at most 18 on a base of length `L` whose last column has even height, each counted +1 or −1 by the parity of its number of blocks ([[hardin-word-identity](pages/hardin-word-identity.md)]). It also counts the skylines of width `n − 1` with every column of height 1 to 5 and tower spacing at least 2, meaning every run of empty cells in a row between two filled cells has length at least 2; these need not reach height 5, so they are the castles of every height up to 5 with that spacing ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)]).

## Catalog

### Castles

Definition: a skyline `(c_1, …, c_w)` with `1 ≤ c_i ≤ h` for every `i` and `c_i = h` for some `i`: width `w`, height `h`; every other family is a set of castles unless its definition says otherwise ([[castle-polyomino](pages/castle-polyomino.md)]).

| the number of strips of width `w` under the plastic rule of height 3: skylines `(c_1, …, c_w)` with every `c_i` in `{1, 2, 3}` in which a column of height 1 is followed by one of height 3, a column of height 2 by one of height 1, and a column of height 3 by one of height 1 or 2 ([[castle-strip](pages/castle-strip.md)], [[reachable-field-census](pages/reachable-field-census.md)]). ### Tree castles

Definition: a castle whose castle graph is a tree: no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2 ([[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)]).

Read left to right, the column heights of a tree castle are a composition of `n` (an ordered sum of positive parts) with no two neighboring parts at least 2, and every such composition is a tree castle | `n = 1…` | `1, 2, 4, 7, 12, …` from `n = 1` | - |  | [A005251](https://oeis.org/A005251) (`= A005251(n+2)`) |

| the number of castles of area `n` (`n` cells), counted up to mirror image, whose sandpile group is trivial ([[sandpile-group](pages/sandpile-group.md)], [[sandpile-census](pages/sandpile-census.md)]). The sandpile group of a castle comes from its castle graph (cells as vertices, joined when they share a side) with sand leaving through a sink, one cell in the sink model and the whole bottom row in the tide model; in both models it is trivial exactly when the castle graph is a tree, that is, for the tree castles, in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2. So this counts the tree castles of area `n` up to mirror image, `(A005251(n + 2) + A000931(n + 6))/2` by Burnside's lemma, the palindromic ones numbering `A000931(n + 6)` ([[castle-graph](pages/castle-graph.md)]) | `n = 1…` | `1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 22, 37, 63, 108, 186, 322, 559, 973, 1697, 2964` | `(A005251(n+2) + A000931(n+6))/2` |  | [A005683](https://oeis.org/A005683) (`= A005683(n+2)`) Twopins positions (the formula agrees with the b-file for `n ≤ 38`)[^sandpile] |

### Palindromic tree castles

Definition: a tree castle with `c_i = c_{w+1−i}` ([[padovan-families](pages/padovan-families.md)]).[^sandpile]

The tree castles are the castles whose sandpile group is trivial, and the palindromic count enters the count of those castles up to mirror image, `(A005251(n + 2) + A000931(n + 6))/2` ([[sandpile-census](pages/sandpile-census.md)]) | `n = 1…` | `1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 16, 21, 28, 37, 49, 65, 86` | `A000931(n+6)` | [A000931](https://oeis.org/A000931) (`= A000931(n+6)`) Padovan |

### Fibonacci-word castles

Definition: a Fibonacci castle whose tower (row 2 read as a 0/1 string) occurs in the infinite Fibonacci word, the limit of `0 → 01`, `1 → 0` from `0` ([[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)]).[^fibsub]

| object | from | first terms | g.f. / formula | OEIS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the number of Fibonacci-word castles of width `w`: Fibonacci castles (height 2, no two neighboring columns of height 2) whose tower, the second row read as a string with 1 for a cell and 0 for an empty place, occurs somewhere in the infinite Fibonacci word `0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, …`, the limit of `0 → 01`, `1 → 0` started from `0` ([[fibonacci-castles-sub-families](pages/fibonacci-castles-sub-families.md)]). The Fibonacci word is Sturmian, with exactly `w + 1` distinct pieces of each length `w`, and from `w = 3` none of them is all zeros, so the count is `w + 1` from `w = 3`, growing linearly | `w = 1…` | `1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9` | `w + 1` for `w ≥ 3` (Sturmian complexity) | - (linear) |

They are half the balanced binary words of length `w` | `w = 1…` | `1, 2, 4, 7, 12, 18, 27, 38, 52, 68, 89, 112` | `A005598(w)/2`, `~ w³/(2π²)` | [A049703](https://oeis.org/A049703) (`= A049703(w)`) |

### Convex castles

Definition: a castle whose skyline is unimodal: `c_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ c_p ≥ ⋯ ≥ c_w` for some `p`; equivalently every row is one run, or exactly `h` blocks; the stacks of polyomino theory ([[convex-castle](pages/convex-castle.md)]).

| the number of convex castles of semi-perimeter `s`, of any width and height, the semi-perimeter `s` being half the length of the boundary, which is the width plus the number of blocks ([[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)]); a convex castle is a castle whose skyline rises weakly to its tallest column and then falls weakly ([[convex-castle](pages/convex-castle.md)]). A convex castle of height `h` has exactly `h` blocks, so `s = w + h` and the count is the sum of `C(2h + w − 3, w − 1)` over `w + h = s`, the Fibonacci number `F_{2s−3}`; these are the stack polyominoes that Delest and Viennot count by perimeter | `s = 2…` | `1, 2, 5, 13, 34, 89, 233` | `t²(1-t)/(1-3t+t²)` | `φ²` | [A001519](https://oeis.org/A001519) (`= A001519(s−1)`; Delest-Viennot's stacks by perimeter); `F_{2s−3}`, the anti-diagonal sums of `C(2h + w − 3, w − 1)`[^semiper] |
| the number of convex castles of semi-perimeter `s` that have an even number of blocks, the semi-perimeter `s` being half the length of the boundary, which is the width plus the number of blocks ([[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)]); a convex castle is a castle whose skyline rises weakly to its tallest column and then falls weakly ([[convex-castle](pages/convex-castle.md)]). A convex castle of height `h` has exactly `h` blocks, so these are the convex castles of even height | `s = 2…` | `0, 1, 3, 7, 17, 44, 116, 305, 799, 2091` | `t³(1-t)/((1-3t+t²)(1-t+t²))` | `φ²` | -[^semiper] |
| the number of convex castles of semi-perimeter `s` with an even number of blocks minus the number with an odd number of blocks, the semi-perimeter `s` being half the length of the boundary, which is the width plus the number of blocks ([[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)]); a convex castle is a castle whose skyline rises weakly to its tallest column and then falls weakly ([[convex-castle](pages/convex-castle.md)]). It is a signed difference, and it repeats `−1, 0, 1, 1, 0, −1` with period 6 | `s = 2…` | `-1, 0, 1, 1, 0, -1` (period 6) | `-t²(1-t)/(1-t+t²)` | periodic | -[^semiper] |
| the number of convex castles of area `n`, the number of cells, of any width and height; a convex castle is a castle whose skyline rises weakly to its tallest column and then falls weakly ([[convex-castle](pages/convex-castle.md)]). Reading the column heights left to right makes a castle of area `n` a composition of `n`, so these are the weakly unimodal compositions of `n` ([[weakly-unimodal-composition](pages/weakly-unimodal-composition.md)]), the stacks of polyomino theory | `n = 1…` | `1, 2, 4, 8, 15, 27, 47, 79, 130, 209, 330, 512` |  |  | [A001523](https://oeis.org/A001523) (`= A001523(n)`)[^classical] |

### m-smooth castles

Height 4 is the diagonal `h = m + 2` for the step bound `m = 2`. A strip need not reach height 4, so this is the anchored 2-smooth castles of height 4 plus the `3^{w−1}` anchored skylines on `{1, 2, 3}`, which all obey the rule | `w = 1…` | `1, 3, 11, 39, 139, 495, 1763` | `(3+√17)/2` | [A007482](https://oeis.org/A007482) (`= A007482(w−1)`; g.f. `1/(1−3x−2x²)`) |

### Zig-zag castles

Definition: a castle with `|c_{i+1} − c_i| = 1` for every `i` ([[zig-zag-castles](pages/zig-zag-castles.md)]).[^zigzag]

Grains sit on the cells, a cell holding at least as many grains as it has neighbors topples and sends one grain to each, and grains that reach the sink vanish; the recurrent configurations form the sandpile group, and in the sink model the sink is one cell ([[sandpile-group](pages/sandpile-group.md)]). | the order of the sandpile group, in the tide model, of the box castle `(2, …, 2)` of width `w`, a 2-wide ladder lying down. Grains sit on the cells, a cell holding at least as many grains as it has neighbors topples and sends one grain to each, and grains that reach the sink vanish; the recurrent configurations form the sandpile group, and in the tide model the whole bottom row is the sink ([[sandpile-group](pages/sandpile-group.md)]). Every 2 × 2 square of cells in this castle rests on the bottom row, the group is cyclic, and its order is the even-indexed Fibonacci number `F_{2w}`; it is a statistic of one castle for each `w` | `w = 1…` | `1, 3, 8, 21, 55, 144` | `a(n) = 3a(n−1) − a(n−2)`, cyclic | [A001906](https://oeis.org/A001906) (`= A001906(w)`) `F_{2n}` (every block on the ground) |
| the order of the sandpile group, in the tide model, of the box castle `(h, h)` of height `h`, a 2-wide ladder standing up. Grains sit on the cells, a cell holding at least as many grains as it has neighbors topples and sends one grain to each, and grains that reach the sink vanish; the recurrent configurations form the sandpile group, and in the tide model the whole bottom row is the sink ([[sandpile-group](pages/sandpile-group.md)]). Only the lowest 2 × 2 square of cells in this castle rests on the bottom row, and the group is cyclic; it is a statistic of one castle for each `h` | `h = 1…` | `1, 3, 11, 41, 153, 571` | `a(n) = 4a(n−1) − a(n−2)`, cyclic | [A001835](https://oeis.org/A001835) (`= A001835(h)`; one block on the ground) |

### Prime castles

Definition: a castle with no column of height 1; its padded form `(1, X, 1)` is a prime of the gluing monoid of castles that begin and end at height 1 (the moated castles of [[castle-classification-shape](pages/castle-classification-shape.md)]) ([[prime-castles](pages/prime-castles.md)]).

| object | from | first terms | g.f. / formula | growth | OEIS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| the number of prime castles of semi-perimeter `s`: castles with no column of height 1 ([[prime-castles](pages/prime-castles.md)]), graded by `s`, half the length of the boundary, which for a castle is its width plus its number of blocks ([[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)]). Removing the bottom row of a prime castle leaves a castle with the same width and one block fewer, and every castle arises once this way, so for `s ≥ 3` these are the castles of semi-perimeter `s − 1`, `A082582(s − 1)` (the row-deletion bijection, [[deutsch-elizalde-2016-bargraphs-cornerless-motzkin](pages/deutsch-elizalde-2016-bargraphs-cornerless-motzkin.md)] §3.9) | `s = 2…` | `0, 1, 2, 5, 13, 35, 97, 275, 794, 2327` | `t·B(t)` | `τ²` | [A082582](https://oeis.org/A082582) (`= A082582(s−1)`; for `s ≥ 3`; the row-deletion bijection, [[deutsch-elizalde-2016-bargraphs-cornerless-motzkin](pages/deutsch-elizalde-2016-bargraphs-cornerless-motzkin.md)] §3.9)[^semiper] |
| the number of prime castles of area `n`, the number of cells: castles with no column of height 1 ([[prime-castles](pages/prime-castles.md)]). Read as compositions of `n`, they are the compositions into parts at least 2, which number the Fibonacci number `F_{n−1}`. They are prime for gluing: castles that begin and end with a column of height 1, glued at a shared column of height 1, factor uniquely into padded prime castles `(1, X, 1)` | `n = 2…` | `1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21` | `q²/(1−q−q²)` |  | [A000045](https://oeis.org/A000045) (`= A000045(n−1) = F_{n−1}`; compositions into parts `≥ 2`)[^prime] |
| the number `U(n)` of prime convex castles of area `n`: convex castles (columns rise weakly to a maximum and then fall weakly) with no column of height 1, which are the weakly unimodal compositions of `n` into parts at least 2 ([[prime-convex-castles](pages/prime-convex-castles.md)]). Removing the runs of height-1 columns at the two ends of a convex castle leaves its prime part, so `U(n)` is the second difference of `A001523`, the convex castles by area; the generating function is `Σ_k q^k/((1−q^k)(q²;q)_{k−2}²)` | `n = 2…` | `1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 19, 28, 42, 61, 90` | `Δ² A001523`; `Σ_k q^k/((1−q^k)(q²;q)_{k−2}²)` |  | -[^prime] |
| the number of prime castles of area `n` (castles with no column of height 1) that are not convex, so that their columns do not rise weakly to one maximum and then fall weakly: `F_{n−1} − U(n)`, all the prime castles of area `n` minus the prime convex ones ([[prime-convex-castles](pages/prime-convex-castles.md)]). The first is `(3, 2, 3)`, at area 8 | `n = 8…` | `1, 2, 6, 13, 28, 54, 106, 194` (from `n = 8`) |  |  | -[^prime] |
| the triangle of the number `U(n, w)` of prime convex castles (convex castles with no column of height 1) of area `n` and width `w`, read by rows `n = 2, 3, …` with `w = 1, 2, …` in each row. Removing the bottom row matches them with the convex castles of area `n − w` and width `w` ([[prime-convex-castles](pages/prime-convex-castles.md)]) | `n = 2…` | rows `1; 1; 1,1; 1,2; 1,3,1; 1,4,3; 1,5,5,1` | convex castles of area `n − w`, width `w` |  | -[^prime] |

The OEIS entry counts the compositions whose alternating parts weakly decrease; the match is checked for `n ≤ 1001` against the two b-files | `n = 2…` | `1, 2, 4, 7, 12, 20, 32, 51, 79` | `Δ A001523` |  | [A342528](https://oeis.org/A342528) (`= A342528(n−1) = A001523(n) − A001523(n−1)`, checked for `n ≤ 1001` against the two b-files)[^prime] |

Padding a castle `C` to `(1, C, 1)` and cutting it at every inner column of height 1 gives its prime factors `(1, X, 1)`, with `X` empty or a castle with no column of height 1, and two castles count once when one is the other's factors in another order ([[signed-prime-castles](pages/signed-prime-castles.md)], [[prime-castles](pages/prime-castles.md)]). ### Tower-spacing castles

Definition: a castle with tower spacing at least `g`: in every row, each run of empty cells with filled cells on both sides has length at least `g` ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)]).

| object | from | first terms | g.f. / formula | growth | OEIS |

| the number of skylines of width `w` with every column between 1 and 2 and tower spacing at least 2: in every row, each run of empty cells that has filled cells on both sides is at least 2 columns wide ([[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)]). Such a skyline need not reach height 2, so this counts the castles of width `w` and of every height up to 2 with that spacing; the castles of height exactly 2 among them number this count minus 1, the flat row `(1, …, 1)`. The gap map followed by the complement carries the tree castles of area `w + 1` (castles in which no two neighboring columns both have height at least 2) one to one onto these skylines ([[a005251-bijection](pages/a005251-bijection.md)]) | `w = 1…` | `2, 4, 7, 12, 21, …` from `w = 1` | the gap map, then the complement, `w = n − 1` |  | [A005251](https://oeis.org/A005251) (`= A005251(w+3)`) |

### Kolmogorov castles

Definition: the skyline `c_i = 1 + |a_i − b_i|` (`i = 1, …, 2n + 1`) of a merged order of two samples, with each peak marked `X` or `Y`; a marked castle, whose skylines are the Dyck-path castles of odd width ([[kolmogorov-castles](pages/kolmogorov-castles.md)]).[^kolmogorov]

### Von Neumann castles

Definition: `vN(n)`, the castle of the ordinal `n`: `castle(∅) = (1)`, and `castle(x)` is a bottom block carrying the castles of the members of `x` in increasing order, with one empty column between neighbors ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]).[^vonneumann]

| object | from | first terms | g.f. / formula | growth | OEIS |

| the width of the von Neumann castle `vN(n)`, the castle of the ordinal `n = {0, 1, …, n − 1}`, where the castle of a set is a bottom block carrying the castles of its members left to right with one empty column between neighbors, for example `vN(2) = (2, 1, 3)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]). It is a statistic of one castle for each `n`; `vN(0) = (1)` has width 1 | `n = 1…` | `1, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, 127` | `2^n − 1`; `vN(0)` has width 1 | `2` | [A000225](https://oeis.org/A000225) (`= A000225(n)`) |

It is a statistic of one castle for each `n` | `n = 0…` | `1, 2, 6, 16, 40, 96, 224, 512` | `(n + 1)2^{n−1}` for `n ≥ 1` | `2` | [A057711](https://oeis.org/A057711) (`= A057711(n + 1)`) |
| the number of blocks (a block being a maximal run of cells in one row) of the von Neumann castle `vN(n)`, the castle of the ordinal `n = {0, 1, …, n − 1}`, where the castle of a set is a bottom block carrying the castles of its members left to right with one empty column between neighbors, for example `vN(2) = (2, 1, 3)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]), with `C(n, d)` of them in row `d + 1`, the nodes of the binomial tree of order `n`. It is a statistic of one castle for each `n`; since `2^n` is even for `n ≥ 1`, every `vN(n)` from `n = 1` has an even number of blocks | `n = 0…` | `1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64` | `2^n`, the nodes of the binomial tree of order `n` | `2` | [A000079](https://oeis.org/A000079) (`= A000079(n)`) |

### Ackermann castles

Definition: `ack(m)`, the castle of the set with code `m`, its members in increasing code, where `code(x) = Σ_{y ∈ x} 2^{code(y)}` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]).[^vonneumann]

| the number of castles of hereditarily finite sets with `b` blocks, a block being a maximal run of cells in one row. A hereditarily finite set is a finite set whose members are hereditarily finite, down to the empty set. Its castle is a bottom block carrying the castles of its members from left to right, in increasing Ackermann code, one empty column between neighbors, and the empty set's castle is the single cell `(1)` ([[von-neumann-castles](pages/von-neumann-castles.md)]). Distinct sets have distinct castles and each block is one pair of braces of the set written out in full, so these are the sets with `b` pairs of braces, the rooted identity trees with `b` nodes | `b = 1…` | `1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 6, 12, 25, 52, 113` | the block tree | [A004111](https://oeis.org/A004111) (`= A004111(b)`) |

## Footnotes

[^1]: Verified by execution (Python 3.11 with SymPy, 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-22; Python 3.10, 2026-10-27, for the rows checked by `bin/python/zig_zag_castles.py` and `bin/python/sequence_catalog_rows.py`, run logs beside them): every row with listed terms recomputed by enumeration, transfer matrix or dynamic program at the ranges stated under each table; every cited A-number fetched from oeis.org and compared with the computed terms at the stated offset.
[^nnacci]: Every row agrees with enumeration of compositions for `n ≤ 14` and with the OEIS data at the stated offset, 2026-10-16.
[^motzkin]: Every row agrees with a transfer-matrix count for `w ≤ 24` or with enumeration for `s ≤ 16`, and every A-number row with the OEIS data at the stated offset, 2026-10-16. All castles by semi-perimeter, `A082582`, are cornerless Motzkin paths and are equinumerous with skew Motzkin paths; they are among the rows by semi-perimeter in the section *Castles*. Their first five terms `1, 2, 5, 13, 35` agree with `A005773`, and the sixth differs, 97 against 96.
[^castles-wh]: The `A(w, h)` rows and the convex row agree with brute-force enumeration for `w ≤ 7` and with the OEIS data at the stated offset, 2026-10-27.
[^semiper]: Every row agrees with enumeration for `s ≤ 16` and with the series of its g.f., and every A-number row with the OEIS data at the stated offset, 2026-10-16; [[castle-perimeter](pages/castle-perimeter.md)] checks the series through `s = 30`.
[^classical]: Every row and formula agrees with enumeration of compositions for `n ≤ 15`, 2026-10-16.
[^blocks]: The `h = 3` rows and the rows by area agree with enumeration for `w ≤ 8` and `n ≤ 15`, 2026-10-16.
[^sandpile]: Every row agrees with Smith normal forms of the reduced Laplacians of all castles with at most 16 cells, in both models, 2026-10-16.
[^hub-parity]: Every row agrees with enumeration for `n ≤ 20`; the OEIS has no match for the even row from `n = 2` to 13 or the odd row from `n = 1` to 13, 2026-10-25.
[^tree-area]: Every row agrees with enumeration for `n ≤ 15` and with the OEIS data at the stated offset, 2026-10-16.
[^fibsub]: Every row agrees with enumeration of the towers for `w ≤ 14`, 2026-10-16.
[^euler]: Every row agrees with `bin/python/euler_castles.py`, and every row with an A-number agrees with the OEIS data at the stated offset over the range the script checks, 2026-10-28.
[^ridge]: Every row agrees with a transfer-matrix count for `w ≤ 24`, 2026-10-16.
[^smoothm]: Every row agrees with a transfer-matrix count for `w ≤ 24`, 2026-10-16.
[^pell]: Every row agrees with a transfer-matrix count for `w ≤ 24`, and every A-number row with the OEIS data at the stated offset, 2026-10-16.
[^disparate]: Every row agrees with `bin/python/hilbert_castles.py`, by transfer matrix and by brute force wherever `h^w ≤ 2·10^6`, and the A-number row with the OEIS data at the stated offset, 2026-10-28.
[^zigzag]: Every row agrees with `bin/python/zig_zag_castles.py` and with every term of the OEIS data field at the stated offset, 2026-10-27.
[^hilbert]: Every row agrees with `bin/python/hilbert_castles.py` and with every term of the OEIS data field at the stated offset, 2026-10-28.
[^mersenne]: Every row agrees with `bin/python/mersenne_castles.py` and, where it has an A-number, with every term of the OEIS data field at the stated offset, 2026-10-28.
[^totient]: Every row agrees with `bin/python/totient_castles.py`, and every row with an A-number agrees with the OEIS data at the stated offset over the range the script checks, 2026-10-28.
[^vonneumann]: Every row agrees with `bin/python/von_neumann_castles.py` and with every term of the OEIS data field it checks at the stated offset, 2026-10-28.
[^konigsberg]: Every row agrees with `bin/python/konigsberg_castles.py`, and every row with an A-number agrees with the OEIS data for `h ≤ 12`, 2026-10-28.
[^orbital]: Every row agrees with `bin/python/orbital_castles.py`, and every row with an A-number agrees with the OEIS data at the stated offset over the range the script checks, 2026-10-31.
[^prime]: Every row agrees with enumeration of compositions for `n ≤ 15`, 2026-10-16.
[^spacing]: A tower-spacing skyline with spacing `g` is one whose heights minus 1 are the window-`g` running minimum of some array, so the `(h, g)` count is Hardin's count of "0..(h−1) arrays, each element the minimum of `g` adjacent elements", proved on [[tower-spacing-castles](pages/tower-spacing-castles.md)]. The `h = 3` row is Hardin's table [A217883](https://oeis.org/A217883), the `h = 4` row [A217954](https://oeis.org/A217954), and the `g = 3` column [A228461](https://oeis.org/A228461). Every cell agrees with the OEIS data at the stated offset for `w ≤ 24`, and its minimal recurrence order, found by Berlekamp-Massey on 90 terms, is `(h − 1)g + 1`, 2026-10-16.
[^kolmogorov]: Every row agrees with `bin/python/kolmogorov_castles.py` and with every term of the OEIS data field at the stated offset, 2026-10-28.
[^brick]: Every row agrees with brute-force enumeration of the walls for `w ≤ 10` and with a column sweep over the 1-histograms beyond, and every A-number row with the OEIS data at the stated offset, 2026-10-29. The OEIS has no match for the even-block or the signed counts at heights 3 to 6, tabulated on [[brick-wall-castles](pages/brick-wall-castles.md)], 2026-10-29.
[^keystone]: Every row agrees with brute-force enumeration of the castles for `w ≤ 6` and with a sweep over the Schröder paths beyond, and every A-number row with the OEIS data at the stated offset, 2026-10-29. The OEIS has no match for the castles by height, the even-block rows at heights 2 and 3, the castles of height 3, or the castles of height 2 by cells, 2026-10-30.
